title: PR traffic sentinel: statistically-sound token-throughput regression gate
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a PR-gating job ("PR Traffic Sentinel") that runs lightweight, statistically-sound performance checks against a rolling baseline to catch token/sec and latency (p95) regressions before merge. Goals: 1) keep PR feedback time under ~20min for typical changes, 2) detect regressions >= 5% on tokens/sec or >= 10% on p95 with confidence, 3) minimize false positives from CI noise and transient cluster variability. Scope: CI job definition, selection of statistical test and aggregation strategy, baseline maintenance (rolling window + commit fingerprints), tooling to store artifacts (benchmarks + traces) and display deltas in PR UI. Out of scope for this ticket: end-to-end production chaos testing and shard-level kernel tuning.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI job runs for every PR and returns pass/fail with a short human-readable delta summary. 2) The job compares candidate run to a 7-day rolling baseline derived from the default benchmark harness for the affected model(s). 3) Regression detection uses a non-parametric or bootstrap approach with configurable alpha; default alpha=0.01. 4) Results (raw samples, statistical summary, docker image hash) are uploaded to S3 and linked in PR. 5) False positive rate on historical canary runs <= 2% when using the default config.
notes: We will reuse existing microbenchmark harness (token_throughput_runner) but add deterministic load patterns and short warmup to reduce variance. Combine median of samples with a trimmed-mean for reporting. Threshold gating supports relative and absolute delta. Implement CI-level opt-out label for very noisy infra changes.
comments: 2026-02-25 Aisha K: Created initial spec after pairing with infra to discuss achievable CI turnaround time. Proposed 3-sample per-run x 5 runs pattern (total ~15 measurements) with 30s warmup. Draft linked: https://confluence.redwood/PR-Traffic-Sentinel-Spec

2026-02-27 Ben L: Ran initial canary on infra-stage (gpu-pool-3). Observed high variance for longer sequences (2048 tokens) — p95 variability ~12%. Decision: limit PR job to representative short/medium sequences (64/512) to keep CI time reasonable and variance low; plan separate nightly long-seq regression job.

2026-02-28 Aisha K: Implemented bootstrap-based delta test (paired bootstrap on per-request throughput) and added fallback to Mann-Whitney U if samples are small. Default rejection threshold set to p<0.01 and relative delta>5%. Added cosmetic PR summary generator (comment template) that can display both absolute and relative deltas.

2026-03-01 Ben L: Opened draft PR with job config and runner changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-harness/pull/512. CI job spins up warmed containers, runs 5 samples per sequence length, and uploads artifacts to s3://redwood-ci/perf/ENG-21540/.

2026-03-02 SRE review (Danielle M): Noted that current container teardown occasionally leaks NVML contexts; added a follow-up subtask to fix teardown (ENG-21541). Also requested that job requests ephemeral GPU labels to avoid noisy hosts. Marked as blocker until teardown fix merged for reliable nightly runs.

2026-03-02 Product feedback (Ravi P): Agreed with short-sequence gating but requested an explicit ticket for bridging to release gating (where thresholds may be tighter). Added label 'release-integration' and suggested a dashboard tile for weekly false-positive rate.

2026-03-02 Ben L: Local benchmark on commit abc123 shows candidate -6.8% tokens/sec vs baseline; bootstrap p=0.003 -> gate triggered as expected. Uploaded detailed artifact: https://dashboards.redwood/benchmarks/ENG-21540/abc123

Planned next steps: 1) fix teardown leak (ENG-21541), 2) instrument runner to emit per-sample latency histograms (prometheus + artifact), 3) wire PR comment bot to post pass/fail and link artifacts, 4) run two-week historical backtest and tune default thresholds to meet acceptance false-positive target.
